title: Hostage
text: “Sadeena, what in the world is this……?”
“……It was placed inside my house. I don’t even know when someone came in to leave something like this.”
“This……We need to show it to the lord.”

Incidentally, Older Sister seemed to vaguely sense that I was nearby in stealth mode, I say. Though she hadn’t managed to pinpoint my exact location. She seemed tense, knowing that if she did anything careless, I’d resort to drastic measures.

According to Older Sister, the straightforward approach in times like this was simply to resort to intimidation. This seemed fairly effective for my goal of buying time before they set out to fish. After all, it would be a problem if they carelessly departed and ended up suffering casualties. The idea was that having a culprit with a clearly stated objective would heighten everyone’s caution. Of course, there was apparently a chance it could backfire and spark opinions insisting they go fishing no matter what.
And so, Big Sister’s parent handed over the threatening letter I’d written to Éclair’s parent.
“This is……”
“Damn it! Isn’t this a threatening letter from the culprit!”
“Do they really not want us going out to fish that badly!”
“Seaetto-sama! Are you saying we should just obey the culprit’s demands as-is?”
“Ngh……”
Éclair’s parent groaned, looking troubled.
“Huh? Isn’t there someone missing from all this commotion?”
“Come to think of it, where’s that guy? He seems like the type to be making a fuss, but he’s nowhere to be seen.”
“Bu-bu-boo!”
……and then Keel came rushing over holding a letter. Éclair’s parent unfolded it and his face grew even more tense. The letter contained only a simple demand.
For starters, one person……Consider this a warning. If you go out fishing, I cannot guarantee anyone’s life.

Well……Following Older Sister’s suggestion, I’d randomly knocked out one of the fishermen—someone who looked like Keel’s father wandering around aimlessly—using Sleep Lance while in stealth mode, then bound him and carried him off, leaving the letter wedged in the door of Keel’s house, indeed.
“Bu-bu-buhee? Bu-bu-bu! Boo!”
Keel was making some kind of fuss, but Éclair’s parent furrowed his brow.
“Such a cowardly act! Just who in the world would do something like this!”

I wonder why. I somehow had a vague feeling I’d done something similar somewhere before—but perhaps it was just my imagination? It was hazy, but I felt like I’d done this to Takt once. It felt close to that sort of thing. Incidentally, I’d had Keel’s father sleeping soundly. He’d probably be out for about three days. I’d wake him up and release him when the tide was right.
“Gh……I absolutely cannot forgive anyone who would do such a thing to my people……but with a hostage involved, I can’t act carelessly.”
“Investigate, and find this child’s father as soon as possible!”
“There must be traces left behind somewhere!”
Incidentally, I’d made sure to leave as few traces as possible. Not only had I layered my stealth multiple times, I’d also crossed rivers in flying mode so I couldn’t be tracked by scent.
And so, though vigilance had risen, thanks to the threat’s effectiveness, the departure scheduled for the next day was postponed.

Keel’s father going missing turned out to be extremely effective. A state of high alert was put into effect across the village and the neighboring town. The Demi-Humans and Beastmen combed through the surrounding area as if searching through every blade of grass. A bit troublesome, but I decided to hide the sleeping Keel’s father somewhere farther away.
“Zzz……Zzz……”

His snoring was quite loud. Well, I’d put him in a wooden box and wrapped cloth around his mouth. Even so, he didn’t wake up. ……He was probably Keel’s parent, but he was noisy even while asleep. He had a somewhat aged-looking face. I wonder what your cause of death was in your previous world? He looked like some kind of dog-type Demi-Human—did he go out fishing too, I wonder? Well, I’d return him alive anyway. Just sleep soundly, indeed.
As I looked at the sleeping face of the man who seemed to be Keel’s father……I found myself wondering what Father, from my first world, would think of this.
‘So this is the eccentric parent who raised Keel as a boy.’

That’s the kind of thing he’d probably say. Keel, who goes from pig to dog. Raised with an upbringing other than that of a pig, Keel’s personality had been shaped accordingly. Hmm……Back in my original Japan, there were rare parents who raised their pigs that way too, so this probably wasn’t all that unusual, was it? I recalled there being quite a few pigs raised in strange households. So Keel wasn’t particularly unusual in that regard.

But why Keel managed to gain popularity rivaling Filo-tan’s was truly a mystery. When I asked Father about it, he said it was probably because she had the same kind of purity as Filo-tan……Well, taking Luna-chan’s input into account too, I’ll just conclude there’s some secret to her popularity that’s beyond my understanding.
Anyway, back to the matter at hand—the threat aimed at stopping them from going out fishing had succeeded. But I couldn’t let my guard down yet.

If I had the leeway, I wanted to get things done now while I could, but if they went out fishing the moment I looked away, that would be unbearable. I considered carefully capturing the fishermen one by one. It reminded me of making the fortress crew pay their dues back in the previous loop.

……If I wanted to, I could get it all done in one night, but I had a feeling that if I captured any more people, Older Sister would start calling me out on it. Indeed, even now, amid the tense atmosphere of the village, Older Sister was putting on an act of knowing nothing, though every so often she’d break into a cold sweat while glancing around. If I recalled correctly……Older Sister had mentioned she’d never met Éclair’s parent face-to-face before, but given the current situation, it seemed they’d been formally introduced. It looked like introductions had been made when Big Sister’s parent delivered the letter I’d written. I was watching from a distance, but I strained my ears to listen in on what they were saying.

Transform into Usaunny mode! Then, in stealth mode, I perched on a roof, twitching my ears to listen in. This was Usaunny’s special skill, indeed. It let me pick up sounds with even more pinpoint precision than usual!
“……What in the world could the culprit’s objective be……Hmm.”
Éclair’s parent groaned. The guard, who looked like an aged version of Crocodile Guy in his crocodile form, stood with arms crossed, apparently deep in thought as well.
“Isn’t it obvious! It must be an attempt to sabotage the fish procurement requested by the Wise King of Intellect!”
“That certainly seems highly likely, but……”
At this point, Big Sister’s parent, along with Older Sister, stepped away from the group and moved behind an empty building, wary of onlookers. Just to be safe, I circled around toward them.
“Could we be the cause of this, by any chance? Sadeena, what do you think?”
Oh? That phrasing suggested Big Sister’s parent might have some idea of what was going on. But at that, Older Sister shook her head.
“……I don’t think so. If that were the case, they wouldn’t bother with something so roundabout—they’d come at us directly, by name.”
“I suppose that’s true……but then what could the culprit’s objective possibly be?”
“……What bothers me is that even in sinking the ship, they’ve been moving carefully so no one gets hurt.”
“Just as Sadeena says, this is far too well-arranged to be a coincidence. Certainly, if it were Melromarc’s people, they’d likely not care if there were casualties……”
“There might be……some other reason behind this. I think it’s best not to hastily assume this is some scheme by Melromarc’s people.”
“Hmm……Does the culprit have some particular aim? Just give me an example, anything will do.”

In response to Big Sister’s parent’s question, Big Sister seemed to be steering the conversation precisely because she knew the information from me. If she was going to get in the way of my plan, I’d simply move on to my next measure—but what exactly did she intend to say?
“……I haven’t the faintest idea……Ah, if only a hero who saves people would come help us in a troubling time like this.”
How blatant of you, Older Sister. Well, a roundabout bit of prompting like that wasn’t going to be enough to get me to act, indeed.
